key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical surrogate can learn the lattice Boltzmann BGK collision operator across the full relaxation range without retraining.
engineering_relevance: This could enable practical quantum-assisted fluid simulation by moving the hardest non-unitary collision step into a compact quantum machine-learning model.
method: Parameterized quantum circuits model the collision nonlinearity via partial Fourier-series expressivity.
Data re-uploading expands the representable frequency spectrum and improves surrogate flexibility.
The model is benchmarked against classical BGK dynamics on standard flow tests.
evidence_signal: The surrogate is validated on the Taylor-Green vortex and double shear layer, showing high-fidelity agreement with classical collision dynamics and flow evolution.
watch_item: Performance depends on architectural choices and quantum circuit resources, so hardware noise and scalability may limit near-term deployment.
paper_title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
